races.name: Rod Gaskin Garden Machinery Handicap

runners_data.name: Toyotomi
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist ideally suited to soft ground with strong recent Thirsk third, but needs pace to aim at
runners_data.spotlight: Good third off this mark at Thirsk (6f, good) last week, doing best of those drawn in single figures and that despite meeting some trouble in running; has plenty of form on soft in France; one to take seriously.

runners_data.name: Mister Bluebird
runners_data.comment: 8yo who has been as good as ever this spring, runner-up on last two starts; respected
runners_data.spotlight: 10lb higher than when making all in the corresponding race 12 months ago; two runner-up finishes over 7f, one of them here, this spring; weakened into midfield over 7f at Epsom on Friday; will need a career best to win this race for a second time.

runners_data.name: Solar Aclaim
runners_data.note: Hold-up sprinter whose soft ground form is excellent but quick return from yesterday's Epsom run is concerning
runners_data.comment: Ideally needs soft/heavy; favourably treated off 4lb below last winning mark
runners_data.spotlight: Sprinter who is happiest on slow ground and gave some encouragement returned to 6f on soft at Epsom yesterday, where he finished mid-division having been squeezed out at the start; 4lb lower than for his last win.

runners_data.name: Brosay
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse whose best form came on softer surfaces last season, returning to optimum conditions
runners_data.spotlight: Won 6f handicaps at Windsor and Ascot last summer; dropped down the weights in defeat this season but there have been glimmers of promise and ground softer than good will be of benefit; ran no sort of race at Carlisle eight days ago (in cheekpieces) but his usual blinkers are back on today; Oisin Murphy booked; interesting.

runners_data.name: Seven Questions
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with class edge having Group 3 win on record, 3lb rise after recent Goodwood success manageable
runners_data.spotlight: Ended a two-year barren spell when getting up late in a 5f handicap here 16 days; 3lb higher mark to deal with but he has a Group 3 win on his record and conditions won't faze him; respected.

runners_data.name: Sudden Flight
runners_data.note: Prominent type better on AW but showed improved turf form at Windsor last time, handles good ground better than soft
runners_data.comment: Possibly best to forgive last two efforts; still well treated on AW form
runners_data.spotlight: Better on AW than turf but handicapped accordingly and he ran his best race on grass when third of seven at Windsor 13 days ago (good to firm); down the field in two runs on soft but his Ayr Silver Cup effort wasn't too bad; new cheekpieces could give him a lift.

runners_data.name: Sturlasson
runners_data.note: Prominent 5f specialist making seasonal return, distance stretch to 6f on soft ground questionable
runners_data.comment: Returned to form when 2nd of six at Bath but may prove vulnerable in this hotter contest
runners_data.spotlight: Did well for new yard last autumn, winning three times (5f, AW/good to soft), and he has run some solid races in defeat in 2026; this will be just his third run at 6f and others bring more pressing claims.

runners_data.name: Jungle Drums
runners_data.note: Prominent runner returning from 10-week break with poor recent form for current yard
runners_data.spotlight: Generally struggled for this yard but the notable exception came when dead-heating at Chelmsford last October (6f, AW); beaten 19l at Doncaster on his return ten weeks ago; not a solid option.

runners_data.name: Fleetwater
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare effective over 6f but 9-week absence and preference for faster ground concern
runners_data.comment: Wasn't disgraced in a stronger race over C&D nine days ago; considered down in grade
runners_data.spotlight: Both wins at Windsor but she is effective elsewhere; runner-up in two of her three starts this year but she's back from nine weeks off and could prove vulnerable.

races.paceDynamic: With Mister Bluebird withdrawn, this becomes a pace scramble with Seven Questions, Sudden Flight, Sturlasson and Jungle Drums all wanting prominent positions in a small field. The early pace will be moderate rather than fierce, but the crucial move will come 2f out when the prominent quartet try to kick simultaneously. The lack of genuine early speed means the race will develop into a sprint finish, but those who secure good early position will have the tactical edge. This pace shape strongly favours prominent runners who can secure position without effort and hold-up horses who can find gaps in the straight.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Battle Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If the four prominent runners establish clear order early without interference
scenarios.body: The pace stays controlled until 2f out when Seven Questions and Sudden Flight can utilise their superior tactical speed from ideal positions. Hold-up horses get swamped by the sustained drive of those already in contention.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Prevail
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent quartet clash for position and compromise each other 2f out
scenarios.body: Toyotomi and Brosay benefit from the pace collapse ahead, sweeping through tired leaders with superior finishing kicks. Solar Aclaim and Fleetwater also profit from the strong gallop.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses Early
scenarios.trigger: If none of the prominent horses show early speed and create a crawling pace
scenarios.body: The race becomes a pure sprint from the 2f marker where class tells and Seven Questions' Group 3 ability shines through. Sturlasson's 5f specialist speed also becomes decisive in a dash.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Traffic Chaos Unfolds
scenarios.trigger: If the small field bunches dangerously in the straight creating interference
scenarios.body: An outsider like Fleetwater or Jungle Drums who gets a clear run benefits while fancied runners get hampered. The pace becomes irrelevant as positioning and luck determine the outcome.

watchPoints.text: Seven Questions could prove too classy if securing uncontested lead from the prominent pack
Toyotomi needs clear running room in straight as Daniel Tudhope will be coming late and wide
Sudden Flight's turf improvement at Windsor needs confirming on much softer ground today
Jungle Drums showing any early sparkle would indicate significant improvement from long break
Pace development in first 2f crucial as moderate early tempo will favour different profiles than sustained gallop

races.name: British Stallion Studs EBF Novice Stakes (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)

runners_data.name: Bulletsnap
runners_data.comment: Yard in great form so must be considered on debut
runners_data.spotlight: 85,000euros foal; second foal; by Minzaal; dam French Listed-placed 7.5f-8.5f winner (including 2yo/AW; RPR 93), sister to useful French 1m-1m4f winner Anobe; betting should be revealing for a stable in fine form.

runners_data.name: The Harv
runners_data.spotlight: 65,000euros yearling, £260,000 breeze-up 2yo; second foal; half-brother to Listed-placed 5f 2yo winner Awraad (RPR 78); dam 5f/6f winner (including 2yo/AW; 88); Irish trainer saddled a winning 2yo newcomer on Wednesday; Oisin Murphy booked; of obvious interest.

runners_data.name: Mobadir
runners_data.comment: Early February foal by No Nay Never; the oldest runner in the field; respected yard
runners_data.spotlight: Left trailing over 1f out on his Salisbury debut (5f, good) 24 days ago, dropping out to finish last of the six runners (Oakford a neck and one position ahead in fifth); can do better and 6f should suit.

runners_data.name: Asgar
runners_data.comment: Early foal; stable often gets them ready first time; makes plenty of appeal on pedigree
runners_data.spotlight: Smart pedigree but in need of the experience when down the field in a 6f maiden at Newbury last month (good ground; 12-1); this looks less demanding and he is open to improvement.

runners_data.name: My A'Ali Baba
runners_data.comment: March foal; 32,000gns yearling, £23,000 breeze-up 2yo; market likely to be a fair guide
runners_data.spotlight: Looked an unlikely winner for the first 4.5f of his Chepstow debut (6f, good to soft) but the penny dropped in the closing stages and he ultimately ran out a decisive winner; the bare form is nothing special and he will need more to defy a penalty but he is open to improvement.

runners_data.name: Oakford
runners_data.spotlight: In need of the experience when fifth of six at Salisbury (5f, good) 24 days ago, finishing a neck in front of the reopposing Mobadir; open to improvement over this extra furlong.

races.name: Goodwood Horseracing Club Membership Selling Stakes

runners_data.name: Cavan Lady
runners_data.note: Unraced daughter of a 7f/1m winner making debut for Richard Hughes, total unknown quantity but well-bred enough to be competitive first time out
runners_data.spotlight: 25,000gns yearling; fourth foal; half-sister to winners Nibras Angel (7f; RPR 96) and Doha Bu Thaila (Qatari 6.5f-10.5f); dam 7f/1m winner (78), sister to 5f-7f winner Munfarrid, half-sister to Listed-placed 6.5f 2yo/1m winner Morning Post; useful pedigree for one starting out in selling company; betting to guide.

runners_data.name: Beach Ahead
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer on debut who needs stronger pace than this small field likely to provide, but showed promise at Windsor on faster ground
runners_data.spotlight: Never a threat but it was still a promising start to his career when fourth of 12 in a 6f maiden at Windsor two weeks ago (good to firm); quickly drops into selling company and he is open to improvement but others have achieved more.

runners_data.name: Leucothea
runners_data.note: Natural front-runner with Oisin Murphy booked, failed as favourite twice but gets significant class relief dropping into a seller
runners_data.spotlight: Beaten favourite in maidens at Bath (5.7f, firm) and Wolverhampton (6f, AW) but she hasn't run badly on either occasion; has the speed to cope with 5f and Oisin Murphy booked now she drops into selling company.

runners_data.name: Fortunate
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who showed marked improvement at Chester last time, can sit handy to Leucothea and may have more progress in her
runners_data.comment: Poor form in her three starts and she looked a hard ride latest; easy enough to swerve
runners_data.spotlight: Poor form on her first three starts but she showed much more when fourth of 12 in a Chester seller (6f, good) eight days ago, prominent throughout and only losing second in the closing stages; now has something to build on and can go well back at 5f.

runners_data.name: Undercover Affair
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with most consistent recent form, but needs pace to aim at and may find this race develops too slowly for his style
runners_data.comment: Leading form claims now dropping into a seller; draw not ideal but can't discount
runners_data.spotlight: Promise in all four starts, keeping on for second in a 6f seller at Chester eight days ago (passed the reopposing Fortunate, who was better drawn, close home); untried on slower than good; leading form claims.

races.paceDynamic: Leucothea will take this race on from the front with no genuine pace pressure from the small field. Fortunate may sit prominent but won't challenge for the early lead, while Beach Ahead and Undercover Affair are hold-up horses who need the pace to develop. With soft ground potentially dulling the kick of closers and only one willing pace-setter, this sets up perfectly for front-runners and prominent racers who can get first run on the field.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Leucothea Wire To Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Leucothea breaks cleanly and settles into an uncontested lead
scenarios.body: She can dictate fractions on the soft ground and kick clear when Oisin Murphy asks, with the hold-up horses needing more pace to aim at than this small field will provide. Front-running tactics prove decisive over this stiff 5f at Goodwood.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Fortunate or Cavan Lady can track Leucothea and get first run
scenarios.body: The tracker gets into contention turning for home and has enough left to reel in the leader, benefiting from the perfect stalking trip behind the pace-setter. Leucothea's recent defeats suggest she may not have the class edge to hold off a closer.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold Up Success
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is stronger than expected and creates enough tempo
scenarios.body: Undercover Affair or Beach Ahead can use their finishing kick to sweep past tiring leaders, with the soft ground not completely negating their turn of foot. The 5f distance just gives them enough time to mount their challenge.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Shock Debutant Win
scenarios.trigger: If Cavan Lady shows immediate ability on debut and gets the right tactical ride
scenarios.body: The newcomer benefits from having no exposed form to beat and gets the perfect education trip in a small field, with Finley Marsh able to position her ideally. Her breeding suggests she should handle the trip and going.

watchPoints.text: Leucothea's jumping - if she misses the break badly she loses her main tactical advantage and this becomes a completely different race
Cavan Lady's market support - any strong betting moves would suggest connections expect her to be competitive on debut
Fortunate's early positioning - she's shown best form when prominent so needs to avoid getting too far back in this small field
The pace through the first two furlongs - if it's genuinely fast it could set up the closers, if slow it confirms front-runner bias
Undercover Affair's draw and early tactics - Billy Loughnane may need to be more positive than usual given the likely lack of pace

races.name: Weatherbys/British EBF Agnes Keyser Fillies' Stakes (Listed Race)

runners_data.name: Botagoz
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with strong recent form who should relish the expected pace scenario and soft conditions
runners_data.spotlight: Won novice events on first two starts, latterly at Nottingham (1m, good) in April; good third of seven in Listed race at York (1m, good) last month, with major late gains from out the back to suggest this longer trip will prompt further improvement; it is needed but she is one to consider.

runners_data.name: Rose Ghaiyyath
runners_data.note: Classic hold-up type with Group 1 entries suggesting high ability, proven on soft ground
runners_data.spotlight: Has Group 1 entries in Coronation Stakes (1m) and Irish Oaks (1m4f); won newcomers' event at Deauville (7f, soft) last August and a rallying fourth in the Group 2 May Hill at Doncaster (1m, good to soft) on her only other race as 2yo; never-dangerous tenth of 19 at 50-1 in the 1,000 Guineas at Newmarket (1m, good to firm) on reappearance but she stuck to her task, beaten about 6l, and should stay 1m2f; a leading contender, including on form.

runners_data.name: Sacred Ground
runners_data.note: Another patient ride specialist from powerful stable, good record on testing surfaces
runners_data.comment: 2nd in two Newmarket Listed races; better form claims than most and still some potential
runners_data.spotlight: Probably acts on good to soft; won debut and runner-up in Listed events on all three starts since; this season's were over 1m2f at Newmarket (good to firm) and Newbury (good) and the latest form makes her one of the top two in this field on ratings; should be bang there again.

runners_data.name: Light Of Paris
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who needs to press Venetia early to have tactical impact
runners_data.spotlight: 500,000gns yearling by Sea The Stars; made a low-key debut on Kempton AW (1m3f, AW) in April but always prominent when winning a steadily run, seven-runner maiden at Ascot (1m2f, good) one month ago in tidy fashion; should improve again but this demands much better even though the second and fifth won maidens next time.

runners_data.name: Capichera
runners_data.note: Non-runner, prominent style would have suited if participating
runners_data.comment: Form stacks up well; appears to have a workable opening mark; respected
runners_data.spotlight: Quiet improver though her four starts have not yielded a win; 1m handicap second off a mark of 80 last time (good to soft) gave hope for 1m2f but surely she has too much to find at this level.

runners_data.name: Plaid
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse improving rapidly but untested on ground softer than good
runners_data.comment: Improving filly; second in Kempton handicap in March; big shout nudged up 1lb
runners_data.spotlight: Has improved a chunk with each of her four runs, last time winning off a handicap mark of 75 at Hamilton (good; unraced on softer) on the step up from 1m to 1m1f; as that win was easily by 8l, she has put herself into serious each-way calculations at this much higher level.

runners_data.name: Venetia
runners_data.note: Lone pace-setter returning quickly from 16 days ago, key to how race unfolds
runners_data.comment: Made all at Ascot on handicap/seasonal debut and looks the type to progress further
runners_data.spotlight: Made all at Ascot (1m2f, good to firm) on handicap/seasonal debut and set steady pace when second here (1m4f, good; unraced on softer) 16 days ago; steady improver but needs a big step forward in today's first-time headgear.

runners_data.name: Ourbren
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner with solid soft ground form but modest recent efforts
runners_data.spotlight: Pretty useful form in Listed races on last two starts as 2yo and she duly won a Bath maiden this April; never-dangerous sixth of ten in Group 2 German 1,000 Guineas (1m, soft) latest is her best form and this new trip is not out of the question, but others have accomplished more and/or shown more potential.

runners_data.name: Della Pace
runners_data.note: Patient ride type who showed best form when fourth in C&D Listed recently
runners_data.comment: Ran well in AW handicap on reappearance; this is a much stiffer task
runners_data.spotlight: 2yo maiden winner whose best form (from six races) came when fourth of eight in a C&D Listed race (good) two weeks ago; slowly away at 40-1 that day and made late progress, so still looks capable of a bit better; that could still mean minor honours, though.

runners_data.name: Lady Dora Mae
runners_data.note: Prominent racer unproven on soft ground, tactical wild card
runners_data.comment: Progressing and likeably consistent; dug deep to finish the job off at Windsor (1m)
runners_data.spotlight: Not proven on softer than good; ridden by Jack Callan (who can't claim in this race) on last four outings; won three of her eight races, including over 1m at Windsor on penultimate start, and best form when upped to 1m2f for second at Nottingham on latest; that handicap form, however, leaves her with major work to do.

races.paceDynamic: Venetia is the lone confirmed front-runner and will set a measured tempo from the gates, likely unchallenged through the early phases. Light Of Paris and Lady Dora Mae can press from prominent positions but both lack the pace to apply serious pressure to Venetia's lead. The soft ground at 1m2f suggests stamina will tell late, with the bulk of this field comprising hold-up horses including Botagoz, Rose Ghaiyyath, and Sacred Ground who will look to time their challenges. This race shape strongly favours the hold-up horses who can conserve energy behind the uncontested pace and finish powerfully when stamina becomes crucial.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Dominant
scenarios.trigger: If the pace remains modest as expected with Venetia unopposed early
scenarios.body: The hold-up brigade gets an ideal tactical setup to unleash finishing kicks when it matters most. Botagoz, Rose Ghaiyyath, and Sacred Ground all benefit from patient rides and superior class telling late.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Venetia Steals It
scenarios.trigger: If no horse can match her sustained gallop and she finds enough in reserve
scenarios.body: Her uncontested lead becomes decisive as the chasers fail to bridge the gap on testing ground. The front-runner's stamina holds up better than expected against tired finishers.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Press
scenarios.trigger: If Light Of Paris and Lady Dora Mae force a stronger early gallop
scenarios.body: The increased pace compromises Venetia's stamina advantage while setting up the race for horses with tactical speed. This scenario creates a more even contest between prominent and hold-up runners.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Drama
scenarios.trigger: If Venetia sets an extremely slow tempo that becomes a sprint finish
scenarios.body: The race becomes a pure speed test over the final two furlongs rather than a stamina examination. Fresh legs and tactical positioning in the home straight become paramount over sustained galloping.

watchPoints.text: Venetia's stamina reserves after recent 16-day turnaround could determine if the pace scenario holds
Light Of Paris and Lady Dora Mae's early positioning will show whether they challenge Venetia's lead
Rose Ghaiyyath and Sacred Ground's closing sectional times reveal if the hold-up scenario delivers
Plaid's first run on soft ground tests whether her improvement curve continues on testing surfaces
Botagoz's finishing position from her customary hold-up spot indicates the pace analysis accuracy

races.name: Billy Vigar Handicap (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Across Earth
runners_data.note: Hold-up style with 605 days off the flat but recent hurdles form suggests retained ability
runners_data.comment: Dual hurdles winner late last year; has winning form over this trip on the Flat
runners_data.spotlight: Two hurdle wins late last year and he's held his form pretty well in that discipline, last seen six weeks ago; his last Flat race was in 2024 for his former yard and peak form that year (1m6f win) suggests this is a realistic mark.

runners_data.name: Call My Bluff
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who won here in 2020 but was last in this race last year, made all at Newbury in April
runners_data.comment: Back to life at Newbury latest and has fine record here; returned to serious calculations
runners_data.spotlight: Won here in 2020 but last in this race last year; back to life at Newbury (2m, good; fine on soft) this April, making all in a six-runner race, but a sluggish start immediately put him on the back foot in the Chester Plate (10-1) one month ago and he ended up last of 17; well treated on old form but perhaps needs things to go his own way these days.

runners_data.name: In The Breeze
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer with two wins this year but disappointing last start in stronger company
runners_data.comment: Winning start for Henrietta Knight at Thirsk last month but this is a much stronger race
runners_data.spotlight: Had a 1m4f win for Mick Appleby last September and another for Henrietta Knight at Thirsk this April; however, no show in a more competitive race on latest start, has never won over further than 1m4f and, although probably stays 1m6f, his sole attempt at 2m (final start last term) was not persuasive.

runners_data.name: Hermetic
runners_data.note: Prominent style with dual soft ground wins in France last autumn, bold fourth on British debut
runners_data.spotlight: Dual soft-ground winner (1m4f/2m) in France last autumn, from just four races there; picked up for 105,000euros in November and put up a bold show when fourth of 17 at York (1m4f, good) last month; stuck to his task at 20-1 that day and looks a strong candidate if that run has brought him on.

runners_data.name: Alfred Boucher
runners_data.note: Hold-up veteran who won smoothly at Salisbury last month despite being lightly raced recently
runners_data.comment: Lightly raced since 2022 but on a dangerous mark; watch the market on this return
runners_data.spotlight: Pipped in the 2022 Ebor; he's now a 10yo and very lightly raced in recent seasons but had sunk way down the weights before winning pretty smoothly at Salisbury (1m6f) last month on third start for this yard; bit to prove these days on softer than good; also back up 4lb but stays 2m and still thrown in judged on his old form.

runners_data.name: Maxident
runners_data.note: Confirmed leader with excellent soft ground record and 271 days freshness, 3lb rise looks workable
runners_data.spotlight: Effective here; goes well on testing ground, as he showed again when winning at Ffos Las (1m6f; stays 2m+) in September on latest start; 3lb rise today is far less concerning than a move away from soft or heavy ground; big player if conditions are in his favour.

runners_data.name: Youthful King
runners_data.note: Hold-up style, 6lb lower than last win but struggling this season with apprentice jockey booked
runners_data.comment: 4lb below last winning mark, but has suffered heavy defeats in his last four starts
runners_data.spotlight: 6lb lower than when winning at Sandown (1m6f, good to firm) last June under Jack Dace, who frequently rides him; has not beaten many in his four starts this season, however; has one piece of form at this track (2022) but something to prove on softer than good.

runners_data.name: Russian Rumour
runners_data.note: Hold-up type who can lead, won by 12 lengths on heavy ground last September
runners_data.comment: Course winner who bids a for hat-trick from a 2lb higher mark; much respected
runners_data.spotlight: 10-58 overall for this 9yo, with none of those races at this track; can make the running; won at Ffos Las (2m, heavy) last September (by 12l) and Nottingham (1m6f, good) this May; not far away when third of four at Lingfield 12 days ago in hat-trick bid and has an each-way chance.

runners_data.name: Arc Zoosve
runners_data.note: Non-runner
runners_data.spotlight: Thriving since the cheekpieces went on in December, winning six of his nine starts in them; that includes his last four races and although the big majority of those runs were on AW, he also scored in a seven-runner race over C&D (good; made all) on penultimate outing; not proven on softer than good (well beaten on soft in October) but, after a comfortable AW win last time, he could still have more improvement in him.

races.paceDynamic: Maxident is the only confirmed front runner and will be allowed to dictate a sustainable gallop over this stamina-sapping trip on soft ground. Russian Rumour can also make the running but is more likely to track Maxident early, with Call My Bluff and Hermetic positioned prominently behind the leaders. The lack of genuine pace pressure means Maxident can control fractions and kick for home when ready, while the hold-up horses like Alfred Boucher, In The Breeze and Youthful King will face a difficult task trying to make up ground in testing conditions. This race shape strongly favours prominent runners and the lone leader, as soft ground and steady pace typically blunt late finishing kicks over two miles.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Maxident Controls Uncontested
scenarios.trigger: If Maxident gets an easy lead with no early pressure from Russian Rumour
scenarios.body: The confirmed front runner can dictate ideal fractions and has the class edge with proven soft ground form over the trip. His September win at Ffos Las showed he thrives in these exact conditions and the 3lb rise is lenient.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Battle Develops
scenarios.trigger: If Russian Rumour or Call My Bluff press Maxident from the start
scenarios.body: The increased pace will stretch the field and favour the proven stayers with tactical speed. Hermetic's French soft ground wins and Alfred Boucher's recent Salisbury success give them the stamina edge.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If the pace becomes pedestrian and the field bunches turning for home
scenarios.body: In The Breeze and Youthful King get the perfect setup for their closing kicks despite the testing ground. The soft conditions still make this difficult but a slow pace could negate the ground disadvantage.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider Ambush
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses completely and form gets turned upside down
scenarios.body: Across Earth's hurdles form translates back to the flat or Call My Bluff rediscovers his 2020 course form. The chaotic nature of handicaps allows for surprise results when conditions suit.

watchPoints.text: Maxident getting an uncontested lead as his soft ground form is superior to these rivals
Russian Rumour's early tactics as she could either press Maxident or drop in behind
Alfred Boucher's position turning for home as he needs to be closer than usual on this ground
Jack Dace's handling of Youthful King as the combination has a good record together
Early pace development between the three prominent runners Maxident, Russian Rumour and Call My Bluff

races.name: Tapster Stakes (Listed Race)

runners_data.name: Hamish
runners_data.note: Proven Group 3 winner at this trip with excellent soft ground record but faces traffic concerns from deep position after 225-day break
runners_data.spotlight: 10yo who's won a hatful of Group 3s at 1m4f-1m6f in his long and distinguished career, including at Newbury in October when last seen; has been kept to ground softer than good for a long time; kicked off that 2025 campaign with a win in this race and this star has good chance to repeat the dose.

runners_data.name: Glen Buck
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner making significant step up from handicaps after lengthy absence with minimal recent trainer form
runners_data.spotlight: 7yo who has had only six races, winning four; not discredited in April 2025 (1m2f; best form at 1m4f) when last seen but this graduation from handicaps seems a stiff task and it's also his turf debut.

runners_data.name: Arabian Crown
runners_data.note: Sole pace-setter who can dictate fractions unopposed but needs to prove stamina holds after disappointing 2024 campaign
runners_data.spotlight: 2024 Sandown Classic Trial winner (good to soft) who missed the rest of that season; underwhelming on first four starts last year and ran particularly poorly at Glorious Goodwood (sole visit here) but he ended that campaign by winning narrowly in a four-runner Listed race at Windsor in August; needs to build on that but should stay 1m4f.

runners_data.name: Tenability
runners_data.note: Progressive hold-up type with strong Ascot 1m4f record but must overcome crowded tactical scenario with three other closers
runners_data.comment: Did well last term; his form is not what's required to win this but he brings potential
runners_data.spotlight: Won a novice and three Ascot 1m4f handicaps on varied ground last June-September; pipped a below-form Hamish for second in Ascot Group 3 on final outing last year and resumed his progress when he reappeared with a close third in Newbury Group 3 (1m4f, good) in April; that puts him into very serious contention today.

runners_data.name: Midak
runners_data.note: Only prominent runner to support Arabian Crown early but has struggled since moving from France with distance concerns
runners_data.spotlight: Won his first three races in France last year and started just 9-1 when brought over for the Derby but faded badly into tenth; ran respectably over 1m1f (soft) in October on his only subsequent start for Francis Graffard but an also-ran in the UAE this year over 1m1f (Group 1) and 1m2f (Listed) on both starts since 300,000euros sale in November; plenty to prove.

runners_data.name: Involvement
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner showing career-best recent form but faces severe tactical disadvantage in this pace-light field
runners_data.comment: Retains plenty of ability but has something to find back on home soil
runners_data.spotlight: Missed 2025; started this season at Meydan and Longchamp but returned to British soil with career-best form 16 days ago when a close fourth of nine in 1m2f Listed race at this track; more to prove on softer than good and this is also his first appearance beyond 1m2f, but that latest run gave some encouragement; either way he needs to find a bit extra.

races.paceDynamic: Arabian Crown will set the pace without pressure from the start, with only Midak capable of sitting prominently early. The remaining four runners (Hamish, Glen Buck, Tenability, Involvement) all favour hold-up tactics, creating a distinctly back-loaded field. Arabian Crown's uncontested lead through the early and middle sections will allow him to dictate fractions and conserve energy for the finish. This race shape strongly favours front runners and prominent racers who can avoid the inevitable traffic problems behind.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Uncontested Front Runner
scenarios.trigger: If Arabian Crown gets an easy lead and finds his rhythm
scenarios.body: The Appleby runner controls every section without pressure and kicks clear when the hold-up brigade encounter traffic in the straight. Buick can time his effort perfectly from the front while the closers struggle for racing room.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Traffic Jam
scenarios.trigger: If the quartet of hold-up horses get bottled up turning for home
scenarios.body: Arabian Crown builds an unassailable lead as Hamish, Glen Buck, Tenability and Involvement all struggle for clear runs simultaneously. The pace-setter capitalises on the chaos behind to secure victory.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Class Horse Emerges
scenarios.trigger: If Hamish gets a clean passage and shows his Group 3 winning form
scenarios.body: The veteran's proven ability at this trip on soft ground tells as Marquand finds the right moment to challenge. Hamish's superior class rating and course form gives him the edge in a driving finish.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Progressive Type Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Glen Buck reproduces his best handicap form stepping up in grade
scenarios.body: The lightly-raced Varian runner benefits from his fresh approach after 415 days off and outbattles his rivals. His four wins from six starts suggest untapped potential at this level.

watchPoints.text: Arabian Crown's early fractions - if uncontested he becomes very dangerous but any early pressure could expose stamina doubts
Traffic problems at the two-furlong pole with four hold-up horses (Hamish, Glen Buck, Tenability, Involvement) needing simultaneous racing room
Hamish's fitness after 225 days off - the class horse but needs the run to bring him to peak condition
Glen Buck's ability to handle the Listed grade step-up after 415 days away from handicap company
Midak's willingness to race prominently early rather than dropping back to his comfort zone

races.name: Elston Support Your Local Air Ambulance Handicap

runners_data.name: Diamondonthehill
runners_data.note: Front-running style with solid recent form but facing another hike from handicapper after Musselburgh second
runners_data.comment: Solid AW campaign this winter but he wasn't at his best returned to turf 12 days ago
runners_data.spotlight: Capable of useful form but not easy to win with these days, getting little respite from the handicapper; another solid effort when second at Musselburgh 17 days ago (7f, good) but others appeal more for win purposes.

runners_data.name: Cherry Cobbler
runners_data.note: Prominent runner hit with 8lb rise after Newmarket win but Stuart Williams has strong course record
runners_data.comment: Down in the weights but form has gone wrong way since his promising handicap debut
runners_data.spotlight: Capitalised on his reduced mark when running away with a 7f handicap at Newmarket three weeks ago (good ground); hit with an 8lb rise but he has had few chances at the trip; untested on slower than good.

runners_data.name: Dr Strangelove
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer back to last winning mark with two course wins, soft ground suits based on similar going record
runners_data.spotlight: His two wins have come over 6f but he is fully effective over this extra furlong; back to his last winning mark and he will be a danger to all if the ground is suitable (well beaten in one run on slower than good).

runners_data.name: Blue Prince
runners_data.note: Versatile hold-up type with strong course form, encouraging return at Kempton suggests readiness to strike
runners_data.comment: Non-runner
runners_data.spotlight: Has some strong C&D form; the second half of 2025 was disappointing but he dropped in the weights and his reappearance third at Kempton was a welcome return to form; big player.

runners_data.name: Wobwobwob
runners_data.note: Prominent runner on long losing streak but soft ground record shows three places from fifteen starts
runners_data.comment: Retains a good chunk of ability but the drying ground will compromise his chance today
runners_data.spotlight: Losing run stretches back over two years and neither start this year suggests he is ready to exploit his lowly mark; the prospect of slow ground does pique interest though.

runners_data.name: Rare Change
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer with bad luck at course last year, inconsistent but possibilities off current mark
runners_data.comment: Good spell around this time last year; possibilities if taking well to refitted blinkers
runners_data.spotlight: Had bad luck in running over C&D during an otherwise successful spell around this time last year; inconsistent since but has possibilities off current mark with cheekpieces given another spin.

runners_data.name: Tronido
runners_data.note: Hold-up type capitalising on drop in class, 7lb rise against stronger opposition will test recent Lingfield win
runners_data.comment: Won twice last term but below that form this year.
runners_data.spotlight: Capitalised on the drop to Class 6 company when running away with a Lingfield handicap (7f, good) 19 days ago; the 7lb rise against stiffer opposition should find her out.

runners_data.name: Serenity Dream
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who won here last August off 2lb lower mark, lacks winning punch in stronger company
runners_data.comment: Chance on this winter's AW best but he was well beaten back on turf last week
runners_data.spotlight: Win here last August (6f) came off 2lb lower; several good runs this year, including in a big field at Ascot four weeks ago, but others look stronger for win purposes.

runners_data.name: Dannick
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer and 14-race maiden with no impact this year, cheekpieces addition insufficient to threaten
runners_data.comment: 13-race maiden who returned after wind surgery with a laboured effort over C&D 16 days ago
runners_data.spotlight: 14-race maiden; no impact in his two runs this year (following a wind operation) and the addition of cheekpieces isn't enough to tempt.

races.paceDynamic: Diamondonthehill and Cherry Cobbler will likely dispute the early lead, with Wobwobwob also showing enough pace to track close behind. The relatively small field and soft ground should create a sustainable gallop rather than breakneck fractions. With six of nine runners showing hold-up tendencies, the pace-setters face minimal early pressure, allowing them to dictate terms through steady sectionals. This race shape strongly favours prominent runners and those with tactical pace who can avoid getting caught behind the wall of hold-up horses that will inevitably form.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Runners Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Diamondonthehill and Cherry Cobbler establish a comfortable rhythm without being hassled by the hold-up brigade
scenarios.body: The leaders get first run on the soft ground while the back-markers face traffic problems in a small field. Prominent runners exploit their positional advantage as closers struggle to find racing room.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Tactical Speed Prevails
scenarios.trigger: If Wobwobwob or Blue Prince use their versatility to track the pace rather than drop back
scenarios.body: Smart positioning trumps pure stamina as the pace becomes stop-start, suiting horses that can quicken off steady gallop rather than those needing strong pace. These tactical types get perfect trips while pure hold-up horses meet trouble.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Class Rise Exposed
scenarios.trigger: If the soft ground becomes testing and recent course winners Tronido and Cherry Cobbler find the grade too sharp
scenarios.body: The step up in class tells as horses who won in weaker company struggle against seasoned handicappers with proven course form. Established performers with strong Goodwood records assert their superiority despite weights.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider Ambush
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses completely and becomes a sprint finish where low weights can overcome class deficits
scenarios.body: Light-weighted horses at the bottom of the handicap get their chance in a bunched finish where carrying less weight matters more than proven ability. The race becomes a lottery where any of the hold-up horses can strike.

watchPoints.text: Cherry Cobbler faces 8lb rise after impressive Newmarket win but any market confidence suggests connections expect him to handle the hike
Watch for Diamondonthehill getting easy lead as small field and hold-up horses could allow uncontested front-running
Blue Prince showed encouraging return at Kempton and his course form reads well for this conditions
Dr Strangelove drops back to his last winning mark and his two course wins came in similar soft conditions
Tronido steps up sharply in class after Lingfield win against weaker opposition in seller company
